The test image shows:
- Stem cut open at soil line revealing internal necrosis
- White fungal growth/mycelium on the stem surface near the soil
- Plant completely dead/collapsed with wilted leaves
- Appears to be a crown/stem rot disease

Key candidates: Southern_Blight (white mycelium at soil line), Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt. Let me view one reference from each top candidate.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows:
- Stem pulled from sandy soil, cut open to reveal internal necrosis (yellowish-white discolored tissue)
- White mycelial/fungal growth coating the stem at the soil line
- Completely dead/wilted plant with dried leaves
- Root system visible, also dead

**Reference comparison:**
- **Southern_Blight** (Bugwood_2): Very strong match — same white mycelial mat at the stem base near the soil line, same root crown area involvement, same pattern of plant collapse
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (Bugwood_12): Shows wilting but no visible white basal mycelium — doesn't match
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** (Bugwood_1): Shows bacterial streaming test — different diagnostic feature entirely
- **Verticillium_Wilt** (Bugwood_4): Leaf wilting symptoms, no stem/crown white growth — doesn't match

The white fungal coating at the soil line and the basal stem rot pattern are hallmarks of Southern Blight (*Sclerotium rolfsii*). The sandy soil context is also consistent with this disease's typical habitat.
